**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 22 (the only audit right binding us) already satisfies the playbook's preferred position on every parameter:

| Parameter | Playbook preferred | Agreement |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | Once per 12 months | § 22.1 — "no more than once in any twelve-month period" ✓ |
| Notice | 30 days' written | § 22.1 — "at least thirty days' prior written notice" ✓ |
| Timing | Business hours | § 22.1 — normal business hours, no unreasonable disruption ✓ |
| Auditor | Independent, confidentiality-bound | § 22.1 — off-site where practicable, independent auditor bound by confidentiality ✓ |
| Cost | Vendor's, unless underpayment > 5% | § 22.2 — Vendor bears costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent ✓ |
| System access | None | § 22.2 — Vendor and auditor "may not access Customer systems directly" ✓ |

Two additional checks cleared the planner's open questions:

- **The 5% shift threshold is confirmed** at the preferred (not fallback 10%) level, and the cost shift is limited to *reasonable* audit costs plus the *undisputed* shortfall.
- **Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) is a bare heading** with no substantive paragraphs, so it creates no broader records-inspection or access right that could outflank § 22. A full-text regex sweep for audit/inspect/verif/remote access returned hits only in § 22.

Section 22.3 gives us further protection beyond the playbook baseline: findings are our Confidential Information, usable only to enforce the Agreement; Vendor must furnish the final report; and payment of a shortfall closes out the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error. None of the walk-away triggers (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote system access) is present.
